title: Adaptive privileged-audit tiering and eviction safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need an automated, adaptive ingestion + storage strategy for audit events that prioritizes privileged-actor events (admin/SAML/SSO/RBAC changes) into higher-fidelity index tiers while applying aggressive eviction and compression for low-value telemetry to control long-term storage cost. This ticket scopes the design and a first implementation for prioritized partitioning, TTL policies, and eviction safeguards that integrate with RBAC v2 and the audit ingestion pipeline.
motivation: Recent audits revealed disproportionate storage growth from verbose low-value telemetry which raises costs and slows queries for security teams. At the same time, privileged events must be retained longer and be query-efficient for incident response and compliance. A one-size TTL increases cost or reduces signal. We need tiered retention with explicit safeguards to prevent accidental eviction of privilege-change events.
technical_summary: Add a priority field at ingestion (derived from actor role, event type, and source), route high-priority events to a hot index/partition with longer retention and denser indexing, route medium-priority to a warm tier with optimized indices, and low-priority to a cold/compact tier with aggressive TTL and delta-compression. Implement an eviction guard that consults RBAC v2 metadata and prevents deletion of records tagged as 'privileged' until an explicit retention-lifting workflow or legal hold. Update ingestion pipeline (kafka -> processor -> indexer) to compute priority and set partition/retention metadata. Provide admin console controls to expose current retention buckets and emergency holds.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion assigns priority tag for at least these event types: RBAC role change, SSO/SAML assertion failures, admin API calls, service-account key operations.
High-priority partition maintains 90-day retention by default and supports full-text indexing on actor/resource fields.
Warm tier supports 365-day retention with optimized columnar indices for histogram queries.
Cold tier compresses payloads and has TTL policy configurable to 30/90/180 days per namespace.
Eviction guard prevents automatic TTL deletion for events with the 'privileged' tag unless an operator explicitly overrides with audit trail.
End-to-end latency from ingest -> indexed hot partition does not increase by >15% under normal load.
Dashboard shows per-tenant storage usage by tier and projected 90-day cost impact after rollout.
Security review signoff completed and retention schema documented in Confluence.
A smoke test runbook exists for validating hold/override behavior in a staging environment.
implementation_steps: 1) Schema: Add 'priority' and 'privileged' boolean to audit event schema and to index mappings.
2) Ingest logic: Update processor to derive priority from actor.role (RBAC v2), event.type, and source; tag events.
3) Partitioning: Create three index templates (hot/warm/cold) with retention TTL metadata and different index settings (refresh interval, compression, shard sizing).
4) Eviction guard: Implement pre-deletion hook in retention controller that queries event.privileged flag and blocks deletion unless hold override recorded to operator audit log.
5) Console: Add a retention settings page to show per-tenant tier allocations and emergency hold UI (requires SSO admin rights to operate).
6) Observability: Add metrics (events by priority, per-tier storage bytes, prevented-evictions, held-events-count) to Redwood Console and alert rules for unusual growth.
7) Tests: Unit tests for priority assignment, integration tests for end-to-end routing, and chaos tests for eviction guard under concurrent retention sweeps.
8) Rollout: Canary to 10% of tenants, monitor storage regressions and query latencies, then progressive rollout with migration of hot-priority backfill for 30 days.
9) Documentation: Confluence design doc + runbook + update compliance playbook for security team.
10) Postmortem template prepared in case of any accidental eviction during rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flag behind 'audit-tiering' (development): end-to-end in staging, security review.
Phase 1 - Canary: enable for 10% of tenants and internal orgs; monitor held-events and prevented-evictions metrics for 7 days.
Phase 2 - Progressive: enable for additional 40% after tuning; run cost baseline comparison and adjust cold TTL default.
Phase 3 - Global: enable for all tenants; provide retrospective and migration guidance for large tenants to opt into extended retention for privileged events.
Rollback: feature-flag off and immediate suspension of retention sweeps for affected partitions; escalation path to on-call security infra.
metrics: Storage bytes per tier (hot/warm/cold) per tenant
Projected monthly storage cost delta vs baseline
Query latency for security queries (avg & 95th) against hot partition
risks: Misclassification: false negatives (privileged events classified as low) could lead to unwanted deletions unless held by guard.
Cost: mis-tuned hot retention could materially increase storage costs for high-traffic tenants.
Performance: additional processing at ingest may add CPU/memory pressure to the pipeline.
Operational complexity: more index templates increases maintenance burden for upgrades and scaling.
Compliance edge-cases: legal holds triggered outside the retention controller need consistent integration to avoid accidental deletions.
decisions: Decision 2026-02-18: Prioritize RBAC role and event.type mapping for initial priority rules; defer ML-based heuristics to future work.
Decision 2026-02-24: Default hot retention = 90d, warm = 365d, cold default TTL = 90d but tenant-adjustable.
Decision 2026-03-02: Eviction guard will be enforced at retention controller level, not at storage layer, to allow simpler audit trail and operator override.
